title: Candidate Map Ensemble and Agreement Surface
objective: Produce candidate maps across the unresolved centroid / epoch / codec-family profiles instead of collapsing uncertainty, with a disagreement/agreement surface.

repository_truth.head: de620bb
reused_engine: cwatlas.r1082.calibration_freeze (P19 frozen calibration), cwatlas.r1082.calibration_fit (P18), cwatlas.r1082.spatialization (families), cwatlas.r1082.wilkes (centroid candidates), cwatlas.r1082.stonehenge_anchor (P17), cwatlas.r1082.partition - NOT reimplemented

implementation.one_layer_per: retained family x Wilkes centroid candidate x epoch profile
implementation.agreement_surface: greedy angular clustering of candidate directions + per-component variance (per-cell variance across retained families) + max pairwise dispersion + largest-cluster agreement fraction
implementation.result_type: CANDIDATE_ALIAS_SET when >1 cluster; else CANDIDATE_CALIBRATED_POINT (still a region)

negative_results: Uncertainty is NEVER zero-collapsed: the result carries the complete bounded alias set plus an agreement surface (collapsed_to_point = false throughout).
A candidate map member is at most a CALIBRATED_CANDIDATE / SOFTWARE_RESULT: refuse_candidate_as_measured() raises via claims.refuse_candidate_as_measured.
Landing near an unsealed famous-place catalogue is never rewarded: refuse_famous_place_reward() raises - only the two sealed training anchors calibrate the map.
F1 and F3 map identically, so their members share a cluster - the ensemble surfaces the genuine indistinguishability rather than hiding it.
Training anchors (Wilkes centroid, Stonehenge) are rendered distinctly from holdout candidates (is_training_anchor flag).

claims.statement: For a query route the ensemble emits one candidate map layer per unresolved profile combination and an agreement/disagreement surface, returning the complete bounded alias set instead of a single collapsed pin.

privacy_check: CLEAN - synthetic/public routes, opaque anchor ids, and public coordinates only; no private path literals, no personal identity tokens, no raw private vector or narrative
